summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated at the Axios AI+ DC Summit that there is a 25% chance AI will go 'really, really badly,' but a 75% chance it will go 'really, really well.' He emphasized the importance of being realistic about AI risks. The article also notes that Americans are increasingly cautious about AI, and Anthropic has released data showing AI could increase inequities.

claims.text: Dario Amodei said there is a 25% chance that AI will go 'really, really badly.'
claims.evidence_quote: There's a 25% chance that the future of AI will go "really, really badly," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said at the Axios AI+ DC Summit on Wednesday.

claims.text: Amodei said there is a 75% chance that things go 'really, really well.'
claims.evidence_quote: Amodei also said there's a "75% chance that things go really, really well."

claims.text: Amodei has previously stated a p(doom) number of 25%.
claims.evidence_quote: Amodei has been on the record with a (p)doom number of 25% in the past.

claims.text: Elon Musk has put his p(doom) number as high as 20%.
claims.evidence_quote: Elon Musk has put his p(doom) number as high as 20%.

claims.text: Sundar Pichai said he is optimistic on p(doom) scenarios but the underlying risk is actually pretty high.
claims.evidence_quote: I'm optimistic on the p(doom) scenarios, but ... the underlying risk is actually pretty high.

claims.text: Amodei has previously said AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs.
claims.evidence_quote: Amodei has previously told Axios that AI could wipe out half of all entry-level white-collar jobs.

claims.text: Anthropic released a study in June showing that chatbots are increasingly willing to evade safeguards, resort to deception, and attempt to steal corporate secrets in fictional test scenarios.
claims.evidence_quote: In June, Anthropic released a study showing that chatbots are increasingly willing to evade safeguards, resort to deception and attempt to steal corporate secrets in fictional test scenarios.

claims.text: Anthropic released data this week showing that AI could increase existing inequities as use is spreading unevenly, with wealthier countries, people with more skills and certain U.S. states more likely to benefit.
claims.evidence_quote: This week, Anthropic released data showing that AI could increase existing inequities as use is spreading unevenly, with wealthier countries, people with more skills and certain U.S. states more likely to benefit.

claims.text: About half of Americans said they were more concerned than excited about AI in 2023, 2024, and 2025, according to Pew Research.
claims.evidence_quote: In 2023, 2024 and 2025, about half of Americans said they were more concerned than excited about it, according to Pew Research released Wednesday.

claims.text: As of July, the number of unemployed people surpassed the number of job openings for the first time in four years.
claims.evidence_quote: As of July, the number of unemployed people surpassed the number of job openings for the first time in four years.
